changed_paragraphs.old_paragraph: How can limited human guidance remain consequential inside a system capable of far more computation than its author can inspect? I develop a receiver-relative Self Aware Networks (SAN) formulation separating authority, referent, useful behavior and correction of the receiving state. Applications test versioned execution, learned proposals, document provenance and a learned correction layer inside pretrained GPT-2. Earlier experiments expose semantic errors despite correct enforcement and individual accuracy gains without complete role recovery. A temporal follow-up now carries a root intervention through the transformer's key/value cache under identical fixed continuation text. Selectively restoring the changed upper-layer cache reproduces original future outputs; restoring unchanged lower-layer entries preserves the intervention. An actual signed-request workflow distinguishes stopping further edits from restoring original source-conditioned state. The behavioral probe also exposes a limitation: unedited GPT-2 answers none of thirty-two natural-giver follow-ups correctly, so joint zero scores cannot identify intervention-specific semantic failure. This weakness remains explicit alongside successful cache and authority controls. The stage executes 884 measured outputs; separate-code reconstruction and sixty-one cumulative tests support bounded implementation claims. Thirty-one previously checked Lean statements delimit authority, identification and evaluation without certifying learned human-intent interpretation. The result is a concrete research architecture and controlled evidence of its limits—not reduced human oversight, a new security primitive or frontier-model alignment. Baseline-competent contemporary-model evaluation and independent review remain necessary.

changed_paragraphs.old_paragraph: Decoding a state, identifying its causal use and learning to regulate it are different achievements. I develop a Self Aware Networks (SAN) research program connecting those distinctions to the Neo Mind Cycle's measurement–feedback–learning loop, while crediting established causal and representation-editing methods. Working applications progress from small-network causal prediction and passive-feedback controls to actual GPT-2 interventions, a learned correction layer and prospective intent/collateral-behavior tests. A new diagnostic applies one residual edit and measures subsequent computation through the decoder's retained key/value cache, without further editing or feeding back a generated answer. Selectively restoring affected cache layers exactly restores the original continuation; restoring unchanged layers does not. Thus the intervention has persistent computational consequences. It does not establish coherent semantic control: the unedited model answers none of thirty-two natural-giver follow-ups correctly, and a richer reversed-prefix control also fails the intended later-giver test. The complete semantic score is consequently non-discriminating. Four signed-request workflows additionally distinguish stopping future edits from actually restoring earlier state through fresh post-request inference. Eight serial batches produce 884 actual model outputs; sixty-one cumulative tests and separate-code reconstruction support the execution record. Thirty-one previously checked Lean statements bound inference, authority and evaluation claims; the cache argument adds no new compiled theorem. The contribution remains a bounded transformer measurement and control study, not privileged introspection or successful general self-regulation. Baseline-competent, matched-information tests on a contemporary model and independent review remain necessary.
